'''Laura Johanna van 't Veer''' (born 1957) is a Dutch [[molecular biologist]] and clinical molecular [[geneticist]]. She is group leader molecular pathology for the Department of Pathology and Division of Experimental Therapy of [[Netherlands Cancer Institute|The Netherlands Cancer Institute]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Profile of Laura J. van 't Veer, PhD|url=http://cancer.ucsf.edu/people/profiles/vantveer_laura.3358|website=University of San Francisco|accessdate=2015-02-26}}</ref> van't Veer is now  Leader of the Breast Oncology Program<ref>https://cancer.ucsf.edu/research/programs/breast</ref> and Associate Director Applied Genomics at the HDFCCC.<ref>https://cancer.ucsf.edu/people/van-t-veer.laura</ref> She is also the founder of the company Agendia,<ref>https://agendia.com/</ref> which provides a genomic test that analyzes 70 specific genomes within a tumor to assess the risk of [[breast cancer]].<ref>https://agendia.com/our-tests/</ref>  

== Education ==
Ever since high school van't Veer has always had an interest in biology. Her high school biology teacher, who was doing research at the University of Amsterdam, brought university level education to her which acted as a pivotal moment to her education. At the age of 14, van't Veer found a keen interest in genes. These parts of her youth led van't Veer to pursue a career in medical research.<ref>https://ascopost.com/issues/august-10-2019/how-laura-j-van-t-veer-phd-became-an-expert-in-genetic-testing-for-breast-cancer/</ref> 

She attended the [[University of Amsterdam]] from 1976 to 1984 and received a B.Sc. in biology and M.Sc. in molecular oncology. According to van't Veer, her "entire undergraduate schooling was dedicated to biology".<ref>https://ascopost.com/issues/august-10-2019/how-laura-j-van-t-veer-phd-became-an-expert-in-genetic-testing-for-breast-cancer/</ref> She continued her studies at the [[Leiden University|University of Leiden]] from 1984 to 1989. She would earn her PhD focusing on the study of oncogene activation and tumorigenesis. van't Veer was specifically researching why ovarian cells become malignant. 

== Career ==
In 2003, van 't Veer cofounded Agendia B.V. in 2003, serving as the chief operating officer of Agendia B.V. until June 12, 2007. In this company, she contributed her invention, MammaPrint. The New England Journal of Medicine published a trial on the MINDACT<ref>https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1602253</ref> that 46% of clinically high-risk breast cancer patients can safely avoid chemotherapy treatment according to the low-risk MammaPrint test result.<ref>https://profiles.ucsf.edu/laura.vantveer</ref> She continues her work with the company today as chief research officer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.agendia.com/management/prof-dr-laura-van-t-veer/|title=PROF. DR. LAURA VAN 'T VEER|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=AGENDIA|archive-url=|archive-date=|accessdate=2019-10-23}}</ref>  She was featured in the cover story of the May–June 2006 issue of Cancer World.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Beishon|first1=Marc|title=Laura van 't Veer: the person behind personalised treatments|journal=Cancer World|date=May–June 2006|pages=6–13|url=http://www.cancerworld.org/pdf/1233_06_13_cw12_coverstory.pdf|accessdate=3 March 2015}}</ref>  With her colleagues in the field, she has been awarded a number of patents related to cancer treatment.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patents by Inventor Laura J. Van't Veer|url=http://patents.justia.com/inventor/laura-j-van-t-veer|website=justia.com|publisher=justia|accessdate=3 March 2015}}</ref>  She has been a member of the Science Policy and Government Affairs Committee of the [[American Association for Cancer Research]] since 2014. From 2013 to 2014, she was a member of the Education and Training Committee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aacr.org/AboutUs/Pages/Governance/standing-committees___35BC28.aspx#.VPY5xHzF8Ts|title=Standing Committees|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=American Association for Cancer Research|archive-url=|archive-date=|accessdate=2019-10-23}}</ref>  She has more than 80 peer reviewed publications to her name.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK100158/|title=Appendix BSpeaker Biographical Sketches|last=|first=|date=|website=|publisher=National Academy of Sciences|archive-url=|archive-date=|accessdate=2019-10-23}}</ref>

van't Veer's research focuses on personalized medicine by analyzing the specific genetic makeup of both the individual tumors and patients.<ref>https://www.bcrf.org/researchers/laura-van-t-veer/</ref> The result of this individualization is the opportunity for physicians to treat their patients with the most effective selection of therapy. 

van 't Veer's MammaPrint is a software technology that assesses a cancer patient's risk of recurrence of breast cancer to better triage the need for costly and straining chemotherapy treatment. MammaPrint led van't Veer to win the 2015 European Inventors Award.<ref>https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/european-inventor-award/meet-the-finalists/laura-vant-veer</ref>The societal benefit is reducing the exposure of chemotherapy to patients that do not need it. Agendia was ranked in 2015 as one of the "world’s 14 leading [[molecular diagnostics]] firms by revenue."<ref>https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/european-inventor-award/meet-the-finalists/laura-vant-veer</ref>

== Awards and merits ==
*IARC Medal of Honor, Lyon, France in 2005
*Van der Scheuren award lecture for European Breast Cancer Research, EBCC5 in 2006.
*ESMO Lifetime Achievement Award for Translational Research in Breast Cancer in 2007
*Breast Cancer Research Fund (BCRF-Pink Ribbon US) grant award in 2007 and 2008
*Delivered the First Annual Harry and Edith Gladstein Award, Indiana University, School of Medicine on April 7, 2009, titled "Molecular Profiles of Breast and [[Colorectal cancer|Colorectal Cancer]] in Patient Management" <ref>{{cite web|url=http://medicine.iupui.edu/clinpharm/seminar/gladstein/|website=Indiana University|accessdate=26 February 2015|title=Annual Harry and Edith Gladstein Visiting Professor Lecture Indiana University, School of Medicine, Department of Medicine}}</ref>
* [[European Inventor Award]], in 2015 for her gene-based breast cancer test.
*''Giants of Cancer Care Award'' in 2020 for cancer diagnostics<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 Inductees|url=https://www.giantsofcancercare.com/recipients/2020|access-date=2021-12-12|website=Giants of Cancer Care}}</ref>
